repairSeq: When emotions run high, don't try to settle things on the spot — agree to step apart briefly to cool down.
Stop blaming each other, and just state your own need: 'I need a clear answer right now' or 'I need some quiet time alone right now.'
Even if the conversation stops, set a clear, specific point to reconnect — 'let's finish talking over dinner tonight,' not just 'later.'
Once things have calmed down, instead of relitigating who was right, leave just one simple rule: 'next time this happens, let's just do this.'
repairHelpsA: Leaving a brief signal of connection even while apart, like 'resting well, see you soon'
Giving a concrete return time like 'after I get off work tomorrow' instead of a vague 'later' or 'I'll handle it'
repairHelpsB: Giving explicit space to think things through alone, without rushing an answer or asking why they look upset
The first two minutes when you sit back down at the agreed time — opening with something light and everyday instead of immediately relitigating what went wrong
repairAvoid: Using the other person's inability to answer as a way to weaponize silence as a kind of punishment
Diagnosing and labeling the other's whole personality — 'you're just an avoidant type,' 'it's your personality that's the problem'
One-sided sacrifice where it's always the same person enduring, or always the same person reaching out first to apologize, to keep the relationship going
repairCommit: Even after a big fight, never let a full day pass without reconnecting — send even a very light message to open the door back up.
For decisions involving significant money or an entire weekend, just share your initial thoughts today and reconvene to finalize a day later.
repairObserve: Notice that the 'return time' you promised each other right after a fight is actually being kept more often.
Notice that the intensity of anxious pushing has eased, and the time spent hiding away out of feeling suffocated has gotten much shorter than before.
repairWarn: When this painful loop — fighting over the same issue and shutting down the same way — repeats 3 or more times with no agreement reached
When it's always the same person enduring and the same person giving in, and relationship fatigue builds up unchecked as a result
weekendRisk: Filling the weekend with plans without discussing it, or, on the other end, never making any plans because you're always too tired
weekendAgree: For this weekend, set in advance a 'time together' block and a 'time resting separately' block
weekendLine: Let's spend some time together this weekend, then each rest and recharge the rest of the time.
weekendSig: When plans fall apart or you're too tired to go out, do you ask for understanding in advance instead of getting irritated?

replySig: Is the 'I'll be busy' message actually followed through on around the time promised?

decisionRisk: One person deciding everything and just announcing it without discussion, or, on the other end, endlessly stalling to avoid taking responsibility
